name: Lennard-Jones cluster global minimum, 38 atoms
description: Place 38 atoms interacting through the Lennard-Jones potential (reduced units) to minimise the total energy. LJ38 is the classic hard case of cluster optimisation: the global minimum is a face-centred-cubic truncated octahedron (energy -173.928427, Cambridge Cluster Database) while the icosahedral funnel traps local searches. The evaluator computes the energy exactly; the seed is a cubic lattice fragment.

sources.locator: Wales and Doye 1997, Global optimization by basin-hopping and the lowest energy structures of Lennard-Jones clusters containing up to 110 atoms.
Cambridge Cluster Database (LJ global minima table, doye.chem.ox.ac.uk/jon/structures/LJ/tables.150.html): N=38, point group Oh, energy -173.928427; inspected 2026-09-20.

requirements.datasets: None downloaded; mathematical constructions or locally generated synthetic instances.

evaluation.paper_metric: Local protocol; see candidate contract and source adaptation notes

execution.interface: construct() -> array of shape (N, 3): Cartesian coordinates of N atoms in reduced Lennard-Jones units (sigma = 1). Atoms must be at least 0.5 apart. Score: total Lennard-Jones energy 4*sum(r^-12 - r^-6) over all pairs, minimized. science_chemistry.relax(positions) (L-BFGS local relaxation) is available to candidates.

limitations: The database values are putative global minima found by extensive searches, not proven optima; the reference is reproduced in tests by constructing the fcc truncated octahedron and relaxing it.
Reaching -173.928427 reproduces a known structure; a lower energy would be a new putative minimum and must be verified independently.

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Determine the lowest-energy structure of a 38-atom cluster under the Lennard-Jones interaction model.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Finite-cluster ground states reveal how interatomic interactions and geometric packing shape molecular-scale structures.

papers.title: Global Optimization by Basin-Hopping and the Lowest Energy Structures of Lennard-Jones Clusters Containing up to 110 Atoms
papers.primary_goal: Locate low-energy Lennard-Jones cluster structures, including difficult sizes and structures not previously found in unbiased searches.
papers.task_relation: The paper explicitly solves Lennard-Jones structural minima for sizes up to 110, including N=38; the local task uses the same physical energy minimization. Reaching the cited known structure is reproduction, and the model is an idealized pair potential rather than a specific experimental material.
